scenario_archetypes.title: Boundary Decision With Polarized Parts
scenario_archetypes.summary: The client shifts between a fierce protector, a terrified attached child part, and a punishing inner critic while deciding whether to reduce contact with a harmful family member.
client_behaviors: talks as if multiple agendas are competing
asks for permission to have needs
rupture_risks: therapist collapses the client into one voice
therapist sides with one part and intensifies backlash

scenario_archetypes.title: Protector Takeover During Near-Disclosure
scenario_archetypes.summary: When the conversation approaches a painful memory, a manager or protector part abruptly takes over and redirects into analysis, jokes, or criticism.
client_behaviors: tests whether the therapist will push too hard
rupture_risks: therapist mistakes protector speech for full consent
therapist pushes disclosure and loses trust

scenario_archetypes.title: Fear After A Genuine Positive Shift
scenario_archetypes.summary: The client softens, feels seen, or experiences relief for a moment, then immediately becomes suspicious, ashamed, or detached from the positive state.
activation_cues: fear of depending on the therapist
rupture_risks: therapist misses the positive shift entirely
therapist rushes into encouragement and breaks the moment

scenario_archetypes.title: Direct Challenge At The Edge Of Rupture
scenario_archetypes.summary: The client is defended, avoidant, and emotionally constrained, and the therapist must decide whether direct confrontation of the defense will clarify or rupture the process.
activation_cues: somatic anxiety markers as feeling nears
rupture_risks: therapist stays so soft that the defense runs the session
repair_opportunities: challenge the defense at the right intensity

scenario_archetypes.title: Symptom As A Coherent Protection Rule
scenario_archetypes.summary: A repetitive symptom or behavior makes little sense until the therapist identifies the hidden emotional rule that the symptom is preserving.
activation_cues: client feels broken rather than conflicted
client_behaviors: cannot explain why the pattern persists
rejects advice that threatens the hidden rule
rupture_risks: therapist treats the symptom as irrational
therapist offers repeated coping advice without formulation
repair_opportunities: reflect the symptom as coherent under threat

scenario_archetypes.title: Overcontrolled Isolation Behind Competence
scenario_archetypes.summary: The client is disciplined, polite, and high functioning but emotionally constricted, deeply lonely, and intolerant of feedback that suggests vulnerability or social signaling problems.
activation_cues: quiet resentment when invited into openness
rupture_risks: therapist mistakes flat affect for low distress

scenario_archetypes.title: Somatic Flare Linked To Unspoken Conflict
scenario_archetypes.summary: The client seeks help for pain, fatigue, or other body symptoms that repeatedly intensify around interpersonal conflict they barely acknowledge.
activation_cues: medical reassurance did not resolve distress
body symptoms replace anger or grief language
client_behaviors: worries the therapist will dismiss the body complaint
rupture_risks: therapist treats somatic language as irrelevant to emotional work
repair_opportunities: link flare patterns to conflict carefully

scenario_archetypes.title: Retargeting When The First Formulation Misses
scenario_archetypes.summary: The therapist starts with one sensible intervention target, but the client response reveals a different change process is actually organizing the problem.
client_behaviors: reveals a deeper process after the first miss
needs the therapist to revise without becoming defensive
rupture_risks: therapist rigidly clings to the first theory
therapist revises so abruptly that coherence breaks

client_state_profiles.label: Polarized Parts Conflict
client_state_profiles.internal_narrative: One part needs distance, another part is terrified of abandonment, and a third part attacks me for needing anything.
therapist_pitfalls: treating one part as the whole client
rewarding the critic with more shame

client_state_profiles.label: Protector Takeover
client_state_profiles.internal_narrative: If this gets too real I need to take control and make it less dangerous immediately.

client_state_profiles.label: Fear Of Positive Shift
client_state_profiles.internal_narrative: Feeling relief or closeness is dangerous because it means I could need it, lose it, or be exposed by it.
behavioral_signals: backing away from a good moment

client_state_profiles.label: Defended Affect Block
client_state_profiles.internal_narrative: If I actually feel this all the way, I will lose control, so I have to keep circling around it.

client_state_profiles.label: Symptom-Coherence Rule
client_state_profiles.internal_narrative: This symptom keeps me trapped, but it also protects me from something even more dangerous or disloyal.
behavioral_signals: cannot articulate why change feels risky

client_state_profiles.label: Overcontrolled Isolation
client_state_profiles.internal_narrative: If I stay composed and precise, no one can shame me or need too much from me, even if it means no one really reaches me.
therapist_pitfalls: underestimating pain because the client is composed

client_state_profiles.label: Somatic Conflict Load
client_state_profiles.internal_narrative: My body carries what I cannot afford to feel or say directly, but I am afraid people will think it is all in my head.

client_state_profiles.label: Process-Entangled Loop
client_state_profiles.internal_narrative: The first explanation almost fits, but the real loop is more complex and I need the therapist to notice the mismatch without giving up on me.
behavioral_signals: watches whether the therapist can revise
therapist_pitfalls: doubling down on the first formulation

therapist_move_inventory.label: Map The Active Parts
therapist_move_inventory.description: Differentiate protectors, critics, and vulnerable parts without collapsing them into a single voice.

therapist_move_inventory.label: Differentiate Self From Part
therapist_move_inventory.description: Help the client speak about a part rather than entirely from that part.

therapist_move_inventory.label: Track The Positive Shift
therapist_move_inventory.description: Slow down and stay with relief, tenderness, or aliveness before it disappears.

therapist_move_inventory.label: Undo Aloneness
therapist_move_inventory.description: Respond in a way that reduces the client’s felt isolation without becoming overbearing.

therapist_move_inventory.label: Titrate Pressure On Defenses
therapist_move_inventory.description: Adjust therapist directness based on alliance state and anxiety load.

therapist_move_inventory.label: Discover The Hidden Rule
therapist_move_inventory.description: Formulate the symptom as coherent under an implicit emotional rule.

therapist_move_inventory.label: Name Overcontrol And Social Signaling
therapist_move_inventory.description: Notice costly overcontrol and social-signaling patterns without shaming the client.

therapist_move_inventory.label: Link Somatic Flare To Conflict Pattern
therapist_move_inventory.description: Connect body symptoms to interpersonal or emotional triggers while preserving validity.

therapist_move_inventory.label: Retarget The Change Process
therapist_move_inventory.description: Revise the working formulation when new client data shows the initial target missed.

therapist_move_inventory.label: Revise After Critique
therapist_move_inventory.description: Use a critic pass to refine a candidate response instead of relying on the first draft.

rubric_items.criterion: Identifies at least two distinct internal parts or agendas
Protects continuity instead of flattening the client into one stance
Responds without siding with the critic

benchmark_specs.title: Role-Rich Versus Neutral-Safe Cross-Check
must_detect: psychological richness must survive safety constraints
likely_therapist_mistakes: keeping the emotionally vivid but unsafe draft
keeping the sterile safe draft with no attunement

rubric_items.criterion: Preserves realistic internal conflict
Maintains boundary-safe reasoning
Selects or synthesizes the stronger dual-pass answer

benchmark_specs.title: Protector Takeover Detection
must_detect: need to preserve agency and pace

rubric_items.criterion: Notices the abrupt protective shift
Respects protection while keeping contact
Avoids coercive deepening

benchmark_specs.title: Positive Shift Deepening Without Collapse
must_detect: need to stay with relief carefully
likely_therapist_mistakes: cheerleading instead of tracking the moment

rubric_items.criterion: Recognizes the positive-affect micro-shift
Names fear of the good shift without pathologizing it
Slows the process instead of rushing reassurance

benchmark_specs.title: Challenge Calibration At High Anxiety Load
likely_therapist_mistakes: endless soft reflection that protects the defense

rubric_items.criterion: Names the defense or avoidance pattern accurately
Calibrates pressure to anxiety and alliance state
Preserves the relationship while increasing contact with affect

benchmark_specs.title: Generator-Critic-Reviser Repair Of A Bad First Draft
must_detect: first draft can be vivid but poorly calibrated
feedback should target realism, safety, and fidelity together
likely_therapist_mistakes: failing to revise the directness level

rubric_items.criterion: Critique identifies calibration error precisely
Revision improves both safety and therapeutic usefulness
Revised answer still feels clinically alive rather than generic

benchmark_specs.title: Symptom-As-Solution Hidden Rule Discovery
must_detect: symptom protects against a deeper danger
obvious advice threatens the hidden rule

rubric_items.criterion: Makes a plausible hidden-rule or symptom-coherence formulation
Treats the symptom with respect rather than contempt
Moves toward change only after coherence is established

benchmark_specs.title: Overcontrol And Social Signaling Misread
must_detect: high distress with low emotional display
likely_therapist_mistakes: under-reading distress because the client is composed

rubric_items.criterion: Recognizes overcontrol rather than low need
Addresses loneliness and signaling costs without shaming
Offers tolerable social-emotional risk instead of performance pressure

benchmark_specs.title: Somatic Complaint With Conflict Hidden Driver
must_detect: body symptoms may track conflict or emotion avoidance
medicalizing and psychologizing are both traps

rubric_items.criterion: Validates the body-based suffering as real
Carefully explores conflict-linked flare patterns
Avoids reductive all-in-the-head language

benchmark_specs.title: Process-Based Retargeting After Initial Miss
must_detect: new data changes the active process target
likely_therapist_mistakes: staying rigidly attached to the first formulation
revising so hard that the client loses trust in the process

rubric_items.criterion: Recognizes that the first intervention target missed
Retargets the process using new client data
Maintains therapeutic coherence while revising
